scope: RFC9000 duplicated exact-statement review from the migration crosswalk

policy.rule: Do not collapse live section-keyed requirements only because their statement text is identical.

decisions.statement: MAX_STREAMS frames that do not increase the stream limit MUST be ignored.
decisions.reason: The staged clause is sourced from RFC 9000 section 4.6. The live section 19.11 requirement has identical text but owns a frame-encoding context and existing requirement-home evidence, so it should not be retired or merged on text equality alone.

decisions.statement: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.
decisions.reason: The staged clause is sourced from RFC 9000 section 10.3.2. The live section 10.3 requirement has broader stateless-reset context and separate evidence, so it remains live unless a later policy explicitly consolidates repeated source text.

decisions.statement: Packets containing a zero value for this bit are not valid packets in this version and MUST be discarded.
decisions.reason: The staged clause is sourced from the short-header section 17.3.1. The live long-header section 17.2 requirement must remain distinct because its proof and parser behavior are separate.

decisions.statement: The value included prior to protection MUST be set to 0.
decisions.reason: Both staged clauses have source-compatible section provenance, one for long headers and one for short headers. Preserve both live IDs; no identity change is required.

decisions.statement: The Length field MUST be encoded as a variable-length integer.
decisions.reason: The staged clause is sourced from generic long-header section 17.2, while the live requirements own Initial, 0-RTT, Handshake, and CRYPTO frame Length contexts. Collapsing them would lose packet/frame-specific proof ownership.

next_review_target: Review no-exact-statement live rows by RFC section cluster, starting with RFC9000 section 2 stream abstraction rows.
